headline: Add an E-Ink screen to your phone for just $63 with the XTEINK X3
summary: The XTEINK X3 is a 3.7-inch E-Ink reader that magnetically attaches to your phone, offering a new reading experience at a very reasonable price of $63.
details: The XTEINK X3 is a new 3.7-inch E-Ink e-reader designed to magnetically attach to the back of your phone, offering a unique twist to mobile reading. It's currently available for a very reasonable $63, making it an affordable way to enhance your device.

This ultra-thin and lightweight e-reader measures just 5.1mm thin and weighs 58 grams. It features physical buttons for easy navigation, ensuring a comfortable reading experience without draining your phone's battery.

Beyond reading books, the X3 can also display images, act as a clock, and even function as an NFC card for convenient access to frequently visited places. Its seamless magnetic attachment makes it feel like an integrated part of your smartphone.

The device comes with 16GB of internal storage, expandable via a microSD card for extensive libraries. This special offer won't last long, so interested users should act quickly to grab the XTEINK X3 at its low price.

headline_marked: [[Ternlight: 7 MB embedding model]] runs in browser with WASM for on-device search
headline: Ternlight: 7 MB embedding model runs in browser with WASM for on-device search
summary: This compact model integrates engine, weights, and tokenizer into a 7 MB WebAssembly package, enabling CPU-only, on-device sentence embeddings for applications like searching React docs.
details: Ternlight is a new on-device sentence embedding model, packing its entire engine, weights, and tokenizer into a remarkably small 7 MB WebAssembly (WASM) file. This allows it to run directly within a browser environment, leveraging the client's CPU.

The compact size and WASM implementation mean developers can integrate powerful semantic search capabilities directly into web applications. This enables scenarios like searching extensive documentation, such as the React docs, entirely on the user's local machine without server-side processing.
caption:
